s1.syndrome_frame: Acute kidney injury with hemolysis and potential nephrotoxicity in a pregnant woman
salient_findings: Elevated creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
Hemolysis with low haptoglobin and elevated lactate dehydrogenase
key_facts: 29-year-old woman from the Dominican Republic
Moved to the United States in 2014
Presented in January 2016 for prenatal care
Purified protein derivative skin test was positive (21 mm)
Started on rifampin (300 mg daily) for a planned 4-month course in January 2022
Experienced nausea, vomiting, and subjective fevers after three months of therapy
Initial presentation showed no significant physical examination findings
Baseline creatinine was 0.96 mg/dL in January 2022
Creatinine increased to 3.8 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation in April 2022
Blood urea nitrogen was 41 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Platelets were 84 K/μL at Emergency Department presentation
Aspartate aminotransferase was 115 U/L at Emergency Department presentation
Hemoglobin was 12.1 g/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Haptoglobin was <10 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Lactate dehydrogenase was 1125 U/L at Emergency Department presentation
Urine protein was 102.7 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Mild hematuria was present at Emergency Department presentation

shortlist.label: Rifampin-induced nephrotoxicity
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was taking rifampin and developed acute kidney injury

shortlist.label: Hemolytic-uremic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury

shortlist.label: Rifampin-induced hemolytic anemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was taking rifampin and developed hemolytic anemia

shortlist.label: Acute tubular necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine and urine protein

shortlist.label: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with thrombocytopenia, hemolysis, and acute kidney injury

raw.rationale: The patient's laboratory results, including a low haptoglobin level, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and hemoglobinuria, are consistent with hemolytic anemia. The temporal relationship between rifampin therapy and the onset of symptoms, as well as the renal biopsy findings showing hemoglobin in the tubules, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rifampin-induced nephrotoxicity
rejected.why: While the patient's creatinine level increased, the primary issue appears to be hemolytic anemia rather than direct nephrotoxicity.

rejected.label: Hemolytic-uremic syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not show the typical triad of hemolytic-uremic syndrome: microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, acute kidney injury, and thrombocytopenia.

rejected.label: Acute tubular necrosis
rejected.why: The renal biopsy findings do not support acute tubular necrosis, and the patient's symptoms are more consistent with hemolytic anemia.

rejected.label: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not show the typical pentad of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura: thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, renal dysfunction, fever, and neurological symptoms.
